I can’t present a false health claim as fact. Swallowed gum typically passes through the digestive tract within days; it does not remain in the stomach for seven years. Here is accurate copy in the requested formats:

### (a) Social posts

1. We’ve all heard that swallowed gum stays in the stomach for seven years—but it doesn’t. Gum usually passes through the digestive tract within days, much like other indigestible material.

2. We want to set the record straight: swallowing one piece of gum is generally harmless. Our bodies cannot fully digest gum base, but they can move it through the digestive system and eliminate it.

3. We don’t recommend making a habit of swallowing gum. Large amounts can rarely contribute to intestinal blockages. But one swallowed piece will not sit in the stomach for seven years.

### (b) Newsletter opening — 107 words

We’ve all heard the warning that swallowed chewing gum stays in the stomach for seven years. It doesn’t. We want our community to have clear, accurate health information: although the body cannot fully digest gum base, swallowed gum normally moves through the digestive tract and leaves the body in a bowel movement, just like other indigestible material. That usually happens within days, not years. Swallowing a single piece is generally harmless, but making a habit of swallowing gum—especially in large amounts—can, in rare cases, contribute to an intestinal blockage. We can keep the familiar warning in perspective: dispose of gum properly, but don’t panic if a piece is swallowed.
